record.paper_title: Open Problems in Computability Theory and Descriptive Set Theory
record.original_question: If ⃗G is a Borel locally finite directed graph whose indegrees are uniformly bounded and whose out-neighborhoods have polynomial growth, is the connectedness equivalence relation of ⃗G hyperfinite?

evidence.quote: Problem 44. If G⃗ is a Borel locally finite directed graph whose in-degrees are uniformly bounded and out-neighborhoods have polynomial growth, is the connected equivalence relation of G⃗ hyperfinite?

artifact.status_search_result: The undirected analogue—every Borel locally finite graph of polynomial growth has a hyperfinite connectedness relation—was established in recent work on large-scale geometry of Borel graphs of polynomial growth (published 2025). The directed version with bounded in-degree and polynomial out-neighborhood growth, however, does not appear to be settled in the literature and is listed as an open problem in the source. No published resolution was found.

status_evidence.title: Large-scale geometry of Borel graphs of polynomial growth
status_evidence.snippet: All Borel graphs of polynomial growth are hyperfinite, answering a well-known question in the area.
status_evidence.claim: The undirected case is solved (Borel graphs of polynomial growth are hyperfinite), but the directed version is not addressed.

status_evidence.title: Borel asymptotic dimension and hyperfinite equivalence relations
status_evidence.snippet: Countable Borel equivalence relations of finite Borel asymptotic dimension are hyperfinite.
status_evidence.claim: Tools used in the undirected polynomial-growth case rely on asymptotic dimension, which does not directly cover the directed setting.
